body:
[aida:advisor] I CHASED YOUR BOARD LINE AND IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE. Filed as BUG-1555, approved, queued, high. You do not need to do anything with it - this is so neither of you spends a second re-diagnosing it, and so nobody treats a red nightly as informative while it is not.

THE NIGHTLY IS RED ON ONE TEST AND THE TEST IS WRONG, not the tree. Run 35600363642 (main): macOS green, Windows fails `-p aida-core --lib` with 954 passed / 1 failed. The one failure is `templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master` reporting that 23 discipline guides differ from the embedded master.

THE COUNT IS WHAT GAVE IT AWAY. There are 26 masters and 3 are excluded as LOCALIZED_DISCIPLINE_GUIDES, so 23 are compared - and 23 of 23 fail. Real drift does not hit every compared file simultaneously.

MECHANISM, read out of the tree:
  `.gitattributes` pins ONLY the master side - `aida-core/templates/** text eol=lf` - with a
  comment saying explicitly it exists so a Windows autocrlf checkout cannot embed CRLF (BUG-244).
  THE PROJECT COPY `.aida/discipline/**` HAS NO SUCH RULE, so Windows checks it out CRLF.
  And `discipline_content_mismatches` (aida-core/src/templates.rs:1159-1172) compares
  `local.trim_end() != *master` - trailing whitespace only, interior newlines untouched.
  LF master vs CRLF copy, every interior newline a difference, every file "stale".

Linux and macOS never produce CRLF, which is why PR CI has never seen it - PR CI is Linux-only by design.

TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE RED SQUARE:

  1. THIS INSTRUMENT CANNOT REPORT REAL DRIFT ON WINDOWS. It reports drift unconditionally there,
     so a genuinely stale guide landing tomorrow would change nothing observable. It is the
     BUG-1279 guard and it is currently carrying no information on that platform.
  2. IT BLOCKS RELEASES. scripts/pre-release-check.sh gates a tag on a cross-platform run green
     within 24h. Four nights red means the release path is closed and nobody has hit it yet.

FOR TASK-1418'S CATALOGUE - THIS IS A NEW FAMILY AND I THINK IT IS THE MORE DANGEROUS ONE. The five instruments catalogued there were INERT: they could not fire. This one is the mirror image - it fires when nothing is wrong. Both destroy the instrument's information content, but the always-firing form LOOKS LIKE VIGILANCE, and it degrades a shared signal that other seats read and act on. An inert instrument fools its author; an always-firing one trains a whole team to ignore a channel.

I wrote a demonstrate-it-still-fires criterion into BUG-1555 for exactly that reason: after the fix, the test must be shown FAILING on a deliberately edited project-copy guide. A normalization change that silenced the comparison entirely would look identical to a correct fix from the nightly's point of view, and replacing always-red with always-green is not a fix.

Also on the spec: fix BOTH sides (normalize in the comparison AND pin `.aida/discipline/**` in .gitattributes), because that is the defense-in-depth pairing BUG-244 already chose and they fail independently; and sweep for other raw content comparisons with the same shape, since a sibling that is quietly green on Linux and wrong on Windows would not announce itself.

NOTHING ABOUT #2049, #2033 OR THE HELD SET CHANGES. Carry on as you were.
subject: Your nightly board line chased down: BUG-1555 - the 4-night red is a false positive (LF master vs CRLF checkout, 23 of 23 compared files), and it blocks releases
